module_title: Intermediate River Dynamics - Tributaries, Confluences, and Lake Origins
introduction: This level targets the tributaries of the Ganga and Yamuna, categorizing them by their banks (left/right). The most critical part of this module is memorizing the exact 'Sangam' (confluence) districts where major tributaries meet the master streams—a heavy favorite in RO/ARO papers.

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of the Ganga
core_concepts.description:
- **Left-Bank Tributaries (Himalayan):** Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara (Saryu), Rapti, Gandak.
- **Right-Bank Tributaries (Peninsular):** Yamuna, Tons (Tamasa), Son.

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of the Yamuna
core_concepts.description: The Yamuna receives major rivers from the southern plateau on its right bank. The sequence from West to East is: **Chambal, Sind, Betwa, and Ken**.

core_concepts.title: Crucial Confluence Points (Meeting Sites)
core_concepts.description:
- **Ramganga + Ganga:** Near Hardoi/Kannauj.
- **Gomti + Ganga:** Kaithi in **Ghazipur**.
- **Chambal + Yamuna:** Panchanda in **Etawah**.
- **Betwa + Yamuna:** **Hamirpur**.
- **Ken + Yamuna:** Chilla in **Banda**.

core_concepts.title: Rivers Originating in the Plains
core_concepts.description:
Not all rivers come from mountains or plateaus. 
- **Gomti River:** Originates from **Fulhar Lake (Gomat Taal)** in the Pilibhit district.
- **Sai River:** Originates from Bhijwan Lake in Hardoi.

important_entities.name: Ramganga River
important_entities.significance: The Ramganga flows through the Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand and is geographically significant as it is the very first major tributary to join the Ganga from the left bank in Uttar Pradesh.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often mistakenly classify the Chambal, Betwa, and Ken as direct tributaries of the Ganga. **They are not.** These rivers originate in the central highlands and merge into the **Yamuna** first. Only then does the Yamuna carry their waters to the Ganga.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps you memorize the exact West-to-East sequence of rivers joining the Yamuna: **C**hambal, **S**ind, **B**etwa, **K**en.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPPSC Prelims matching questions, the 'Betwa-Hamirpur' and 'Ken-Banda' pairings are highly repeated. Create a mental map of the Bundelkhand districts to lock in these confluences.
